Origami Wagon — fold mechanism verified; the hinge, the lock, and one geometric limit

Simulation Phases 0–4: intake, kinematics, fold force, deployed loads · 2026-07-12 · built from Wagon OG2.stp + OG Wagon Flat Pattern.dwg

Mechanism1-DOF rigid-foldable herringbone
Deployed stateθ* = 35.85°, on the fold path
Rigid-fold jamθ = 75.2°, rims collide
Collapsed basket≈ 86 mm (3.4″) via compliant squeeze

The fold, end to end

The basket sheet was rebuilt as 26 rigid panels and folded numerically from nearly flat (θ=2°) to nearly stacked (θ=88°). Only the accordion creases are driven; the chevron diagonals follow the mechanism passively. Panel stretch stays below 0.02% through the whole sweep — the pattern is a genuine single-degree-of-freedom mechanism, and the CAD deployed geometry sits exactly on its path (RMS 0.7 mm).

Headline finding

The pattern cannot fold flat as a rigid mechanism — walls jam at θ = 75.2°

Past the deployed state both walls lean inward over the floor. The wall widths (298 + 360 mm) sum to 44% more than the 457 mm floor width, so the opposing rims collide while the bundle is still 216 mm thick. Reaching the stowed thickness (≈86 mm incl. the 26-layer stack) requires ~19 mm of rim overlap — the panels must bow elastically past each other (≈0.1% bending strain, feasible for PP/SRPP). Consequences: a fold-force hump and snap-through in the last ~13° of collapse, spring-back against the latch, and extra bending fatigue at the rim contact. This is the most likely mechanical explanation for the April note that the shape “folds after breaking it in”.

Design law: for jam-free flat folding, left wall + right wall widths must not exceed the floor width. Options: shallower walls (≤228 mm), an extra longitudinal pleat per wall, offset/nesting rims, or accept and engineer the compliant squeeze (Phase 3 quantifies force & fatigue).

Crease pattern, measured and signed

The DWG flat pattern reduces to five parameters: accordion pitch 105.33 mm, chevron column width 61.70 mm, diagonal angle 59.6°, wall panels 298.3/360.0 mm, floor 333.3 mm. Mountain/valley was not assumed — it was measured from signed dihedrals of the deployed STEP body. Kawasaki holds at every vertex; Maekawa gives 3M/1V — locally flat-foldable.

The “~3-inch” figure holds for the basket sheet only. A 0.76 mm sheet (McMaster 5895N113 class) would cut the stack to ~20 mm → basket ≈51 mm (2″), at the cost of stiffness — the supplier’s 50 kg load concern pulls the other way.

Phase 3 — what it takes to close it

The rim jam is mechanically free. Modeling the walls as cantilever plate strips, bowing them 18.5 mm past each other takes under 1 N for every candidate sheet (≤4.4 N even for a 3 mm laminate) at ≤0.04% strain. No snap-through, no fatigue issue — downgrade the jam from mechanism blocker to a cosmetic rubbing detail.

The real closing force is the living hinges. With hinges heat-set at the deployed shape (wagon springs open; latch holds it shut), closing rotates every crease ~100°. Hinge web thickness — set by scoring depth in Adam’s process — controls everything:

hinge web t_hStored energyLatch must holdVerdict
0.4 mm27 J69 N (~7 kg)closable, gentle self-deploy
0.6 mm93 J234 N (~24 kg)too heavy for consumers
1.0 mm430 J1084 Nirrelevant if panels are rigid — see design review update below

Phase 4 — the end-lock under load

The lock is modeled exactly as designed: the shells clamp the end flap bands, holding the end profile rectangular (triangle when folded). Because the mechanism is single-DOF, controlling that one angle locks the whole basket — and the numbers say the lock is the structure:

Case (PP 2.14 mm sheet)Floor sagMid-rim motion
50 kg payload, lock ON, hinge 0.4 / 0.6 / 1.0 mm90 / 72 / 38 mm116 / 92 / 47 mm
100 N down on mid-rim (lock ON, 0.6)48 mm77 mm
100 N inward on mid-rim (lock ON, 0.6)11 mm68 mm — matches supplier’s “top edge collapses”
50 kg, lock OFF (one end free)756 mm — total collapse636 mm

Payload torque at deployed is +15.2 N·m/rad toward folding — load holds the wagon shut against its own spring, but a slipping lock means collapse under load: latch engagement is safety-critical.

Design review update · mobility analysis

Confirmed: locking the end angle makes the basket kinematically rigid

Per design intent (rigid panels, hinges purely kinematic, shape controlled by the wall angle): SVD of the rigid-panel constraint Jacobian shows the free basket has exactly 3 mechanism DOF — the global fold plus the two end flaps — and with both end angles locked, 0 DOF. Hinge stiffness then contributes nothing to load capacity and can be minimized for folding: a 0.2 mm hinge web gives a ~9 N latch and a gentle ~3 J self-deploy, with a conventional lock/unlock at the shells.

What the sheet must supply instead is panel rigidity. 50 kg, ends locked, near-free hinges:

Panel bending stiffnessFloor sagMid-rim motion
bare 2.14 mm PP sheet101 mm132 mm
3×21 mm25 mm
10× (target)5.5 mm6.6 mm
30×1.8 mm2.1 mm

Architecture: panels ≥10× bare-sheet bending stiffness (ribs/beads in molded plastic — consistent with the supplier’s molded-plastic direction — or twin-wall PP), hinge webs ≤0.4 mm (0.2 mm target), end lock as the single structural control. Watch item: panel thickness drives collapsed stack (26 layers); ribs stiffen with far less stack growth than thickness does. Lock reactions ~245 N shear per end at 50 kg — a conventional latch handles it.

Phase 5 — rib layout & the HF test plan

With the end-lock architecture confirmed, the sheet’s job is panel rigidity. Bending energy under the 50 kg case concentrates in the wall panels of the middle bands — the walls are the webs of a folded-plate beam spanning the 683 mm between locked shells. A molded rib section of ~6 × 2 mm at 25 mm pitch (+22% sheet mass) hits the 10× stiffness target; ribs stay ≥15 mm clear of every crease and never bridge a fold.

The full coupon & acceptance plan for HF is in phase5/PHASE5_TEST_PLAN.md. Key lines:

TestSpecAccept

Scoring windowweb 0.2 mm nominalnever exceed 0.4 mm web (latch ≤69 N)
Ribbed panel, 3-pt bend250 mm span, 100 mm coupon≥4.5 N/mm (10× bare sheet’s 0.45)
End lockreacts 15.2 N·m/rad + 245 N shear/end2× proof load 1 h, slip ≤2°; 5,000 cycles

Phase 6 — stack budget; arms deleted, walls do the work

Design decision: the arms are vestigial and removed from the load path. The sheet + end lock carry everything. A targeted stiffening sweep settles where the material must go: floor stiffness is irrelevant to sag (the deployed basket is a folded-plate beam; the walls are its webs, carrying ~88% of the bending energy) — sag is set by the walls alone: 101 mm bare → 9.5 mm at 6× walls → 5.5 mm at 10× walls → 2.7 mm at 20×, with the floor left completely bare in every case.

Stack budget (collapsed bundle vs ~120 mm shell interior): the 16-deep wall-layer columns are the constraint, so wall ribs must nest. Recommended scheme — walls-only 5.8 mm nested ribs (10×), floor bare, molded rim bead: 5.5 mm sag at 50 kg and a ~102 mm (4.0″) bundle — the briefcase closes with margin. (6×/4.5 mm ribs: 9.5 mm sag, 3.6″ bundle, if shallower ribs mold easier.)

Final architecture: end-angle lock (0-DOF) + hinge webs ≤0.4 mm + walls-only nested ribs (10×) + rim bead + bare floor — no arms. Torsion remains a non-issue (the soft hinges comply; creases see ~6 N·mm at a 5° twist). Test plan: wall bend coupons ≥10× bare (4.5 N/mm on the 250 mm span), no floor-bead or arm checks.

Phase 7 — the next-sample build package

Everything above compiled into tooling files: phase7/OG_Wagon_NextSample_v1.dxf + phase7/BUILD_SPEC.md. Layered drawing: cut boundary, mountain/valley score lines (39/39 verified against the deployed STEP dihedrals — mountain scores the outside face, valley the inside), walls-only nested rib layout (5.8 × 2 mm @ 25 mm, half-pitch offset between bands, 15 mm crease clearance), and the rim-bead zones on the crease-free long edges.

Rim check closed at the final spec: 100 N inward push moves the mid-rim 11.7 mm, fully elastic (6.7 mm for a lean-down) — inside the ≤15 mm acceptance before any credit for the rim bead. Predicted sample scorecard: 5.5 mm sag at 50 kg, ~10–20 N deploy force, 4.0″ collapsed bundle.
